description:
## Background

The Issue Explorer coordinator extraction will move race-sensitive listener, navigation, and Settings behavior out of `App`. Existing tests cover most user paths, but several invariants named by the refactor plan are not asserted directly: startup fallback after listener-registration rejection, cleanup of a listener that registered before a later registration failed, preservation of authoritative Issue Navigation state during invalid-view canonicalization, and retention of the underlying Issue Navigation Entry while Settings is open.

Locking these contracts before the wide mechanical move makes the move easier to review and gives failures a clear cause.

Triage: `ready-for-agent`.

## What to build

Extend the existing App-level integration suites so the current implementation proves the lifecycle and Issue Navigation contracts that the coordinator extraction must preserve.

## Technical Approach

- Extend the StrictMode listener controller so transition and refresh registrations can reject deterministically.
- Add a first-registration rejection case: startup Issue loading and Workspace-state reading still dispatch unless the lifecycle was disposed.
- Add a second-registration rejection case: startup still dispatches, and the successful transition listener is disposed exactly once on teardown.
- Extend the invalid Issue List View canonicalization test to assert the final `window.history.state.beadsmithNavigation` entry, including index, route fields, and Workspace path.
- Add or extend an App Settings case showing that the underlying Issue route and Issue Navigation Entry survive while Settings occupies the replacement route.
- Keep these tests at the App interface; do not create a private lifecycle-hook harness or transport port.

## Considerations

- Listener registration remains serial: transition first, then refresh, then startup dispatch.
- A rejected first registration means the second registration is not attempted by the current serial implementation.
- Every successfully registered listener must be disposed exactly once, including late-resolving registrations after teardown.
- Canonicalization must not erase unrelated browser history state.
- Do not change production behavior unless a test reveals that the documented current contract is not implemented; report such a discrepancy before widening the issue.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] First-listener registration rejection has App-level startup fallback coverage.
- [ ] Second-listener registration rejection has startup fallback and successful-listener cleanup coverage.
- [ ] Invalid-view canonicalization asserts the authoritative Issue Navigation Entry, not only the URL.
- [ ] Settings coverage proves the underlying Issue Navigation Entry survives.
- [ ] No private lifecycle test seam, lifecycle port, or in-memory transport adapter is introduced.
- [ ] `mise run verify` passes.

## Test Plan

- Update `src/App.strict-mode-lifecycle.test.tsx` for listener rejection and cleanup.
- Update `src/App.navigation.test.tsx` for canonical history state.
- Update `src/App.settings.test.tsx` only if its existing route-retention coverage does not already assert the required state.
- Run the focused TypeScript test task while iterating, then `mise run verify`.
- No new desktop E2E scenario is required because this issue records renderer lifecycle and browser-history contracts.
title: Lock Issue Explorer orchestration contracts before extraction
